title: Risk posture/governance calls never 400 the whole dashboard when 0 or 2+ projects are in scope
description: Previously, fetchRiskPostureAndGovernance called risk-management-service's risk-center/posture and risk-center/governance with no projectId at all — those RMS routes require exactly one — so every single call unconditionally 400'd and was silently swallowed, leaving postureScore permanently null regardless of project selection. The fix only calls RMS when scopedIds resolves to exactly 1 project.
steps: Call GET /api/dashboard/metrics with no projectIds filter (org-wide, multiple projects)
expectedResult: Both calls return HTTP 200 (never a 400 propagated from RMS); the first has data.risk.summary.postureScore === null, the second has a real numeric postureScore.

title: Vendor assessment pipeline numbers don't zero out for a project-scoped (non-admin) caller
description: vendor_assessments has no reliable projectId of its own (only a handful of stray documents happen to have one). Previously spreading projectScope directly onto a vendor_assessments query silently matched zero documents for every project-scoped caller, zeroing assessmentsOverdue/pipeline.current/inProgress/overdue. Fixed by joining through client_vendors.projectId via $lookup.
preconditions: Non-admin user, member of exactly one project, that project's vendor has at least one overdue assessment
steps: As that non-admin user, call GET /api/dashboard/metrics
expectedResult: data.vendorRisk.summary.assessmentsOverdue and data.vendorRisk.assessmentPipeline.overdue are both > 0, reflecting the real overdue assessment — not silently zeroed.

title: fetchProviderCoverage returns the {provider,count,color} shape FrameworkCoverageCard actually reads
description: Previously returned {provider, frameworks} — a shape FrameworkCoverageCard.jsx's chart/legend never read at all — rendering a zero-height, uncoloured bar with a tooltip reading 'Frameworks: undefined'. Fixed to return [{provider:'Cloud', count, color:'#3182CE'}].
preconditions: At least one ClientControl with cloudPosture.dominantStatus set
expectedResult: Each entry has non-null provider, count, and color fields (e.g. {provider:'Cloud', count: N, color:'#3182CE'}) — never {provider, frameworks} with a missing count/color.

title: Framework Board's readiness summary respects the selected project(s) instead of always being org-wide
description: fetchFrameworkReadiness's ClientFramework query previously never accepted/applied projectScope — always org-wide regardless of the selected project — feeding readyCount/inProgressCount/avgCoverage/strongest/weakest with unscoped data even when the caller had narrowed to one project.
preconditions: Project A has 2 active frameworks; Project B (different project, same org) has a 3rd, unrelated framework
expectedResult: totalActive is 2, not 3 — Project B's framework is excluded when only Project A is in scope.

title: Risk KPI counts read residualRisk.level/treatment.status, not the non-existent riskLevel/riskTreatment.status fields
description: The risk aggregation's critical/high/open counts previously referenced $residualRisk.level and $treatment.status paths that didn't exist under those old names on the risks schema, so every count silently evaluated to zero for every org.
preconditions: At least one risk document with residualRisk.level='Critical' and treatment.status != 'completed'
expectedResult: Both counts are > 0, matching the seeded risk — never silently 0 regardless of real risk data.

title: scopeCacheKey no longer collapses every non-admin's project scope to the literal string '[object Object]'
description: projectScope.projectId can be a plain ObjectId, an {$in:[...]} array (a non-admin's membership set), or absent. Naively stringifying the {$in:[...]} case previously collapsed to '[object Object]' for every non-admin, letting two different non-admins collide on the same Redis cache entry regardless of their actual distinct project access.
preconditions: Two non-admin users in the same org with disjoint project memberships
steps: As User X (Project A member), call GET /api/dashboard/metrics
Immediately as User Y (Project B member), call GET /api/dashboard/metrics
expectedResult: User Y's response reflects Project B's own data, never a cached copy of User X's Project A response.
